- V1.1 capability flag
- Modifying interfaces in fabric/common/channelconfig/api.go

- Upgrade process and reconfiguration transactions

**U2: Read-Your-Writes during key retrieval** - Adding `stub.GetTrxState(key string)` API to chaincode shim to allow accessing updated keys during active transaction.

**U3: Video documentation for adding organizations** - Creating a video tutorial. This is documentation, not software development. Minimal coding effort.

**U4: CouchDB performance knowledge** - Knowing/querying the performance of Fabric queries with CouchDB. Likely requires benchmark testing or documentation.

**U5: MSPConfig as interface** - Refactoring MSPConfig to be an interface to allow constructing channel config blocks outside of configtxgen.

**U6: Remove chaincode singletons** - Refactoring to remove singletons, prerequisite for lifecycle work.

**U7: Test configuration generation** - Setting up tests so that peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml are generated based on World config.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go as the primary implementation language (consistent with the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase).
Implement the Capabilities Framework using three separate capability maps in the channel config: one at the channel (root) level, one at the application level, and one at the orderer level.
Define a single 'V1_1' capability string at each of the three maps for v1.1, encapsulating all non-backwards-compatible behavior changes.
Adopt the 'crash on missing capability' strategy for v1.1 (simple, obviously correct, no graceful degradation required).
Enforce that the orderer group's capabilities are enabled before allowing the application group's capabilities to be enabled, in order to prevent state-database forks during the initial v1.1 upgrade.
Add a new method (e.g., stub.GetTrxState(key string)) to the ChaincodeStubInterface to support Read-Your-Writes semantics during the current transaction.
Refactor MSPConfig to a Go interface with concrete implementations, enabling programmatic construction of channel config blocks outside of configtxgen.
Remove the global chaincode singleton state in the peer and replace with dependency-injected per-test/per-call instances to enable better test isolation.
Drive the peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml test configuration generation from a single 'World' config structure so that all integration test instances are consistent.

Design the new chaincode lifecycle validation parameter interface to return both regular chaincode validation info and a special case for '+lifecycle' with an auto-generated majority-orgs signature policy.
assumptions: A single senior Go developer with deep prior knowledge of Hyperledger Fabric internals is performing the work.
A workday is 8 hours of focused development effort (meetings, code review cycles, and integration are accounted for within each estimate).
The development environment, CI pipeline, and existing test infrastructure are already in place.
No major architectural surprises or cross-component blockers arise during implementation.
All unit tests, integration tests, and documentation updates are included in the per-activity estimates (not added separately).
For U3 (video tutorial), the developer both creates the supporting slides/diagrams and records/edits the video.
For U4 (CouchDB performance), the work is interpreted as designing and running benchmarks and documenting the observed query performance characteristics (not a full performance engineering project).
Code review iteration with other Fabric maintainers is included within each activity's estimate.
The orderer 'pre-flight' enforcement described in U1 is a small, well-scoped change once the capability maps exist (it does not require a separate major design effort).

activities.activity_name: Design and document the Capabilities Framework
activities.activity_description: Review the existing channel config structure, design the three-map capability model (channel / application / orderer), define the V1_1 capability semantics, design the consumer-facing interfaces in fabric/common/channelconfig/api.go, and produce an internal design note.

Add the channel capabilities map to the channel config, implement the ChannelCapabilities interface and its V1_1-backed implementation in fabric/common/capabilities/channel.go, and wire it into channel config initialization and validation.

Add the application capabilities map to the application group config, implement the ApplicationCapabilities interface and its V1_1-backed implementation in fabric/common/capabilities/application.go, and wire it into peer-side config processing (e.g., VSCC, peer gating).

Add the orderer capabilities map to the orderer group config, implement the OrdererCapabilities interface and its V1_1-backed implementation in fabric/common/capabilities/orderer.go, and wire it into orderer-side config processing and chain creation.

activities.activity_name: Implement V1_1 capability string, support checks, and crash-on-missing behavior
activities.activity_description: Define the 'V1_1' capability string constants, implement the support-check logic for each binary (peer, orderer), and add the crash behavior for binaries that do not support a required capability. Include consumption sites for the new interface methods (e.g., SetChannelModPolicyDuringCreate).

Extend the configtx proto and YAML schema to support the three capabilities maps, update configtxgen to emit capabilities into the generated channel config, and ensure config transactions correctly carry and validate capabilities on orderer startup and reconfiguration.

activities.activity_name: Implement orderer pre-flight enforcement of capabilities
activities.activity_description: Add the orderer-side check that prevents the application group from enabling a capability (e.g., V1_1) before the orderer group has enabled it, and add the equivalent down-level-orderer crash guard for future (v1.2+) upgrades.

Add unit tests for each capability map, integration tests for the upgrade scenario (rolling upgrade + reconfiguration), tests for the crash behavior, and tests for the orderer pre-flight enforcement. Cover both happy paths and error paths.

Write developer-facing documentation describing the capabilities model, the upgrade procedure, the process for adding a new capability, and the consumer-side interface pattern. Update relevant Fabric docs.

Add a new method (e.g., GetTrxState(key string) ([]byte, error)) to the ChaincodeStubInterface, implement it on the shim side using the in-transaction write-set overlay so callers can read keys updated during the currently active transaction, and add unit tests plus brief documentation.

activities.activity_name: Create video tutorial for adding organizations to a running network
activities.activity_description: Plan the video script, create supporting diagrams (e.g., a .ppt picture illustrating the reconfiguration flow), record the step-by-step process of adding an org without bringing down the network (configtx, signatures, reconfiguration tx submission), edit the video, and publish it alongside the docs.

activities.activity_name: CouchDB query performance benchmarking and documentation
activities.activity_description: Set up representative Fabric query workloads against a CouchDB state database (rich queries, JSON queries, indexed vs. unindexed), measure and record throughput and latency characteristics, and document the observed performance characteristics and tuning guidance for network managers.

activities.activity_name: Refactor MSPConfig to a Go interface
activities.activity_description: Convert the current MSPConfig struct into a Go interface, move existing concrete behavior into one or more implementing types, update configtxgen and any other callers to depend on the interface, and ensure programmatic construction of channel config blocks outside of configtxgen is possible. Add tests covering the new programmatic construction path.

Identify all package-level singleton chaincode state (registries, handlers, etc.), refactor them to be instantiated per-peer/per-call with explicit dependencies, update all call sites, and update the existing test suite to construct chaincode components per test rather than relying on global state.

activities.activity_name: Generate peer/orderer YAML from the World config in tests
activities.activity_description: Extend the test framework so that, given a 'World' config struct (peers, orderers, orgs, channels), the integration tests automatically render the corresponding peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml files rather than relying on checked-in templates. Add coverage for the new path and migrate existing tests as needed.

activities.activity_name: Implement new chaincode lifecycle validation parameter interface
activities.activity_description: Define and implement the lifecycle interface method that returns the validation parameters for a given chaincode, including the special-case handling for '+lifecycle' itself (auto-generated majority-orgs signature policy). Hook it up to the new lifecycle and add unit tests for both regular chaincodes and '+lifecycle'.

Run an end-to-end integration test pass that exercises all eight user stories together: a v1.1 network upgrade with capabilities enabled, chaincode using GetTrxState, an org added via reconfiguration, CouchDB-backed queries, programmatically built channel config, singleton-free tests, World-driven test config, and the new lifecycle validation interface. Fix any cross-feature regressions.

activities.activity_name: Final documentation, release notes, and cleanup
activities.activity_description: Write the combined release notes covering all eight features, finalize all in-tree and published documentation, address remaining review comments, and perform final cleanup (deprecation notices, comment fixes, doc linting).
